records.specification_basis: The 962C cockpit photograph shows instrumentation on the dashboard behind the wheel and no display integrated into the continuous rim. The exact 1987 article describes the car's wheel and dash but does not identify any wheel display. The full cockpit image shows a continuous upper arc on the wheel; it is not an open-top formula/GT wheel. Because the gallery does not identify the photograph's chassis/year, confidence is not high. The cockpit photograph visibly shows a continuous circular suede rim, and the exact 1987 report refers to the original car's steering wheel. It is not a D-shaped or GT/formula fixed-grip wheel. The visible warning/indicator lamps are on the dashboard, not on the rim; the photographed wheel has no visible wheel-mounted shift-light strip. The image is not a uniquely identified 1987 chassis, so this remains medium confidence. PMR lists a five-speed manual, and the exact 1987 Le Mans-winning 962C report independently says 'Five speed manual.' The exact car is described as a five-speed manual with dogleg first, and the cockpit evidence shows a conventional manual race-car wheel/dash arrangement rather than paddles or buttons. A dogleg first is an H-gate form; it is not a sequential paddle interface. The exact 1987 car's driver report describes the clutch as physically tough, uses the clutch to leave the line, and says it was not fully released until well after the start. Porsche's 962C history confirms this is the manually configured car, not the separate PDK variant.
